calls.headline: Foreigners buy EGP 101.5bn of Egyptian debt in a week, sell EGP 365m of shares
calls.body: In the week to Thursday, foreigners bought a net EGP 101.54bn of Egyptian bonds and bills while Egyptians sold EGP 108.40bn, the EGX's weekly report shows (Maspero, Youm7). In shares, foreigners sold a net EGP 365.4m and Arabs EGP 303.1m, excluding deals, while Egyptians bought about EGP 669m; foreigners are net sellers of EGP 13.36bn of shares this year. Weekly turnover rose 15.1% to EGP 596.7bn. The EGX30 still rose 1.7% to 52,023.37 and the EGX70 EWI 5.5%, and the central bank's dollar rate eased 0.9% to EGP 53.50.
calls.view: Foreign money is coming for the pound's yield, not for Egyptian companies: a one-year bill at 26.07% against 12.7% inflation pays more than any EGX30 dividend, and Friday's rise in US yields to 5.15% did not stop it. That keeps the pound firm into the IMF program's December 15 end, but leaves the EGX30's gains resting on local buyers, which makes the index more exposed to a local rate cut being pushed back than to the dollar.
calls.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 55.50 (central bank sell rate) before December 9.

calls.headline: Bills drew EGP 282bn of bids on Thursday as the pound firmed to EGP 53.50
calls.body: The central bank sold EGP 114.03bn of 182- and 364-day bills on Thursday against a EGP 100bn target, from bids of EGP 282.19bn: the six-month bill yielded 26.07% and the one-year 25.02% (Egypt Telegraph, central bank). The central bank's dollar rate eased to EGP 53.50 from 53.62, a 0.2% gain for the pound, on the day the US 10-year Treasury yield rose about 12 basis points to 5.10% and the dollar index reached 103.18, a new 19-month high (Treasury, Reuters via AsiaOne). Fed funds futures now price a December hike as all but certain (CME FedWatch via CNBC).
calls.view: Demand at 2.8 times the amount sold, with yields steady near 25–26%, says the carry trade is holding even as US rates rise: foreign money is still being paid about 12 points over 12.7% inflation. That keeps the pound firm into the IMF program's December expiry and keeps local rate cuts off the table; the desk keeps the dollar in EGP 52–55.
calls.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 55.50 (central bank sell rate) before December 9.
calls.line: Thursday's auction showed the demand behind the week's debt buying.

calls.headline: Brent ends a second losing week at $95.84 as the IEA sees a surplus
calls.line: Cheaper oil eases the fuel bill, but LNG keeps the gas cuts in place.
calls.body: Brent settled at $95.84 on Friday, about 2.5% lower on the week, after the International Energy Agency said supply would run 1.7m barrels a day above demand this quarter, the first surplus since the war began (Reuters via RTÉ, FinanceFeeds). Iran's navy said on Saturday that three tankers hit mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz; none was named and the claims are not confirmed (AFP via Oman Observer). No new word on Egypt's gas cuts to industry, still 33% for fertilizer plants.
calls.view: A surplus forecast caps oil near $90–100 even with mines in Hormuz, which helps Egypt's import bill; the desk keeps its view that Brent stays below $105, judged November 20. For fertilizer makers the constraint is LNG, not crude, so the gas cuts stay until cargo prices fall.

calls.headline: Juhayna's third-quarter profit rises 33%; stock slips 2.3%
calls.line: Record sales and steady margins, but the stock fell on the call.
calls.body: Juhayna's third-quarter revenue rose 25% to a record EGP 10bn and net profit 33% to EGP 654m, after a EGP 107m currency loss; EBITDA margin widened to 14.7% from 14.3% (earnings call, Investing.com transcript). Management expects the fourth quarter to match the first three and 2027 revenue growth close to this year's, with more price rises planned. The stock fell 2.3% to EGP 24.13.
calls.view: The call confirmed the growth is volume and price, not one-offs, which supports the desk's EGP 27–28 projection by end of January; the fall looks like selling into the news, not a change in the case. Exports fell 11%, the weak spot.
calls.wrong: Juhayna closes below EGP 22 before the end of January.

calls.headline: Chips fall for a second day: AMD drops 8.8%, Broadcom 4.8%
calls.body: AMD fell 8.8% and Broadcom 4.8% on Friday, giving back Thursday's rally after Jensen Huang's exit, and Nvidia lost 2.0% to $162.85, below $4tn in market value (CappNotes, Yahoo Finance). Nebius fell 9.9% after cutting its near-term revenue forecast, about 26% in two sessions, and Dell lost 7.2% and Cisco 6.2%. Technology was the only S&P 500 sector to fall, down 2.0%, while consumer staples rose 1.4% and 314 members rose against 185 that fell. The Nasdaq still gained 2.3% on the week and the S&P 500 2.5%, ending four-week losing streaks.
calls.view: This is money moving inside the market, not out of it: the equal-weight S&P 500 rose 0.2% while the index fell. Thursday's jump in AMD and Broadcom was a bet that Nvidia's customers would switch; Friday's reversal says investors want Nvidia's own numbers first, on Tuesday. The desk's view that chips stay under pressure was judged right on its date, with Nvidia down 20.4%.
calls.wrong: The Nasdaq closes below 24,000 before November 20.

calls.headline: Producer prices rise 0.3%, below forecast; December hike odds near 90%
calls.line: A softer reading did not change the Fed's path, and the 10-year closed at 5.15%.
calls.body: Producer prices rose 0.3% in October against 0.4% expected, and 6.5% from a year earlier, the most since November 2022; core prices rose 0.3%, as forecast (BLS via InvestmentNews, AFP via Yahoo). CME FedWatch put the chance of a quarter-point hike on December 9 at 89.7% and a half point at 10.3%. The 2-year yield closed at 4.88% and the 10-year at 5.15% (Treasury); the 2-year rose about 35 basis points on the week, its biggest weekly jump since September 2024.
calls.view: A hike in December is priced; the question is whether it is one and done. A 5.15% 10-year makes the S&P 500 at about 7,560 dear against bonds, but earnings are still rising, so the desk keeps its view that the index holds above 7,250 into December 9, at medium confidence.
calls.wrong: The S&P 500 closes below 7,250 before December 9.

calls.line: The steady-earner trade held while tech sold off.
calls.body: Consumer staples were the best S&P 500 sector on Friday, up 1.4% (CappNotes). Walmart rose 1.5% to $128.09 and Costco 1.3% to $1,106.21, 14% above its 50-day average, and JPMorgan 1.0% to $346.19. Walmart reports on November 19.
calls.view: The rotation from AI spenders to steady earners that the desk called on October 30 is working: Walmart is up 5.6% since then and Alphabet 4.2%. Costco's RSI of 76 says that one is stretched; Walmart's results are the next test.
calls.wrong: Alphabet and Amazon beat Walmart and JPMorgan from October 30 to November 27.

view.headline: Bills and remittances keep the dollar in EGP 52–55
view.body: The pound firmed on a day US yields jumped, because the bill auction showed foreign and local demand intact: bids of 2.8 times the amount sold at 25–26%. Foreign bill buying and record remittances still outweigh a firmer dollar, so the pound has room to hold near EGP 53–54 into the IMF program's December 15 expiry. The risks are a half-point Fed hike, dearer oil and export dollars lost to gas cuts.
view.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 55.50 before December 9, or a bill auction clears with bids below the amount offered.
